subject: Safehouse MAP: POC onramp checklist & networking preflight
messages:
From: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@atlashealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlashealth.com>, procurements@atlashealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Safehouse MAP kickoff + quick infra questions

Hi Irene and team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AtlasHealth is excited to move into a short evaluation MAP to validate latency and multi-tenant isolation for our patient-facing features. Before we lock dates, a couple of quick infra questions so we can align our security and network teams: 

- We need a clear list of the API key provisioning steps and whether keys are scoped per-environment or per-org.
- What does org setup look like from our side (service accounts, SAML sync) for the POC?
- Can you share a minimal IP allowlist CSV and an expected CIDR for peering?
- Any requirements for peering (AWS accounts, VPC CIDR blocks, cross-account role)?

Goal: start environment provisioning next Tuesday (11/3) and run 7-day perf eval. Doable? If helpful, I can loop in our infra lead.

Appreciate the checklist — Lucas
Lucas Chen
Head of Platform, AtlasHealth
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@atlashealth.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Safehouse MAP kickoff + quick infra questions

Thanks Lucas — all good questions. I attached a short playbook (safehouse-map-poc-playbook.xlsx) and an IP template you can drop into your ticketing system. High level answers below plus a proposed onramp timeline.

Summary answers:
- API keys: we provision two keys for the POC by default — one scoped to the test org (read/write for the evaluation namespace) and one short-lived key for load/ingest tooling. Keys are issued from the Console; we can pre-generate if you prefer.
- Org setup: create a customer org in the Console. We support SAML SCIM for user sync; for a fast POC you can invite 2-3 users; production SAML can be enabled later. Service accounts: we recommend creating one service account for automation; instructions are in sheet 2.
- IP allowlist: attached ip-allowlist-template.csv — add your outbound NAT/egress ranges. We also support per-key CIDR enforcement.
- VPC peering: we support cross-account peering on AWS. Required: VPC CIDR (non-overlapping), account ID, and region. We will request a peering acceptance link once you share those details.

Proposed onramp timeline (short):
1) Day 0 (11/3): Share CIDRs, account ID, and pick two contacts for peering acceptance + service account creation.
2) Day 1 (11/4): Redwood provisions customer org + pre-generates keys; AtlasHealth applies IP allowlist and accepts peering.
3) Day 2 (11/5): Peering active, smoke tests, and sample inference test.
4) Days 3-9 (11/6-11/12): 7-day perf evaluation run; we collect latency/cost and provide a rolling dashboard.

Ask: please confirm the Day 0 date (11/3) or propose alternatives. I can also jump on a 20-min preflight call with your infra team tomorrow.

Attachments: safehouse-map-poc-playbook.xlsx, ip-allowlist-template.csv, vpc-peering-sequence.png

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@atlashealth.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Safehouse MAP kickoff + quick infra questions

Adding a couple of pragmatic notes from the Dedicated/peering side so Atlas can avoid a couple of common blockers: 

- Sequence: please share the account ID and CIDR early. If your CIDR overlaps with our peering pool we'll propose a NAT-forwarded path temporarily while you re-assign ranges. That can add 24–48 hours if not caught early.
- Pre-approve peering from the AWS console (we will email a cross-account peering request). If Atlas has an automated security review, include our peering principal: 123456789012.
- Keys & quotas: the pre-generated POC keys are tagged and have a 50 RPS soft cap by default; if you expect sustained higher throughput, let us know and we can increase quotas for the eval window to avoid throttling affecting latency numbers.
- Cost profiling: for the MAP we will provide a morning snapshot each day with token breakdown by route so you can validate cost per inference.

Irene — I left two TODOs in the attached playbook: (1) confirm whether Atlas wants pre-generation of keys, (2) confirm whether the POC runs in us-west-2 or us-east-1. Rafael
From: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@atlashealth.com>

Irene / Rafael — thanks for the detail and the playbook. Quick confirmations: 

- We will run the POC in us-west-2.
- Account ID: 987654321098. CIDR blocks (egress that will hit Redwood endpoints): 54.212.0.0/16, 44.192.32.0/20 (we also uploaded these to the ip-allowlist-template.csv).
- Please pre-generate the two keys and send them when the org is created — Maya will handle service account invites.
- We can accept the peering request; Maya is the nominated contact for acceptance.

We are set to begin Day 0 on 2026-11-03. Please send the peering request and keys as soon as they are ready.

On the peering principal: if you can include the principal ID Rafael listed in the peering request that will help our automation.

Best,
Lucas
